issues.description: Check directory name does not match metadata CheckID, breaking discovery
issues.detail: The directory and Python class are named `compute_image_not_publicly_shared`, but the PR description and CHANGELOG mention `compute_image_publicly_shared`. The metadata.json CheckID is `compute_image_not_publicly_shared` which matches the directory, so the description is wrong. Verify alignment because Prowler relies on filename==CheckID==class for discovery.

issues.description: Listing custom images without filter will include all public Google images
issues.detail: `self.client.images().list(project=project_id)` returns only images owned by the project, which is correct — but it also returns deprecated/obsolete images. There is no filter on `deprecated.state`, so deprecated images still get IAM-policy calls. More importantly, the check covers ALL custom images including system/family ones; consider scoping or documenting this.

issues.description: Exception handler uses error.__traceback__.tb_lineno which can be None
issues.detail: In `_get_images`, `error.__traceback__.tb_lineno` is accessed on exceptions that may have no traceback (e.g., manually-raised), which would raise AttributeError inside the except block and mask the original error. This pattern is used elsewhere in the file but warrants a guard here since the test fixture raises a bare Exception.

issues.description: IAM-policy failure silently marks image as not publicly shared (false negative)
issues.detail: When `getIamPolicy` raises (e.g., permission denied as in test-image-3), the code logs and continues with `publicly_shared=False`. The image is then reported as PASS, hiding a true positive. Consider surfacing an error/unknown status or skipping rather than reporting PASS based on unverified data.

issues.description: Images fetched serially per project, no threading like other resources
issues.detail: Other resource fetchers in this service use `__threading_call__` for per-region/per-zone parallelism. `_get_images` iterates project_ids sequentially and issues a `getIamPolicy` call per image serially. On accounts with many images and multiple projects, this will be slow. Consider threading per project or per image.

issues.description: Permissions checklist item not addressed in PR
issues.detail: The PR template asks whether new provider permissions are needed. `compute.images.getIamPolicy` is a new API call and may require additional IAM permission beyond the existing compute viewer roles used by Prowler. The PR does not confirm whether the documented minimum permission set was updated.

review.summary: The PR adds a straightforward GCP Compute Engine check for publicly shared custom disk images, with reasonable model, service code, metadata, and unit tests. Main concerns: the IAM-policy fetch failure path silently downgrades to PASS (false negative), the description/CHANGELOG naming appears inconsistent with the actual files, and there is no parallelization for what could be a many-image, many-project workload. Also worth confirming whether new IAM permissions (compute.images.getIamPolicy) need to be added to Prowler's documented minimum role set.
